Speaking after Russia, Ukraine and the US held trilateral talks today in the UAE, US secretary of state Marco Rubio has said the talks were “very productive”, but that there was still a lot of work to be done. Reuters reports Rubio also said that it was a goal at some point to expand the trilateral talks to include other European voices.

Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that the first day of US-led talks in Abu Dhabi between Ukraine and Russia was “constructive and quite substantive”, after being briefed by Kyiv’s negotiators in UAE. “The trilateral format was constructive and quite substantive,” Zelensky said on X, adding that he “gave our team clear instructions for further dialogue – both in the trilateral format tomorrow and more broadly, over the coming days, with envoys of the US President and representatives of Europe.”

Russia ⁠attacked 10 ⁠Ukrainian ⁠regions overnight, hitting five major ⁠energy substations that ⁠transmit electricity between regions, Ukrainian prime minister, Sergii Koretskyi, said. The substations that were hit were in the ⁠Poltava, Dnipropetrovsk, Vinnytsia and Kirovohrad regions, Koretskyi said. Russian attacks killed at least nine people and injured 39 others across Ukraine over the past day, according to a report in the Kyiv Independent.

The European Union will contribute €50m ($55m) to an initiative to improve Black Sea security, EU chief Ursula von der Leyen said Tuesday, after several attacks on ships in the region. A number of vessels were struck in the Black Sea off Bulgaria and Romania in October, leaving more than 30 sailors dead or missing, in suspected spillover from the Russia-Ukraine war.

The EU has said it stands ready “to come with a swift and united response” after France blamed Iran for a spate of cyber-attacks on supermarket freezers and chillers that caused millions of euros of damage. Speaking to journalists on Monday, French foreign minister Jean-Noël Barrot said “Europe-wide sanctions” would be imposed against those responsible as he announced France believed that Iran’s Revolutionary Guards were “responsible for this attack”.

Iran has responded to the accusation by France that it was responsible for the recent cyber-attacks on supermarket fridges in the European country, declaring them “baseless”. AFP reports that in a statement, Tehran said “Iran’s foreign ministry categorically rejects the French government’s baseless and one-sided accusations against Iran regarding alleged cyber activities in France”, adding that it “strongly condemns this hackneyed policy of levelling accusations against the Islamic republic”.

Europe’s manufacturers could give up on attempting to compete with their Chinese counterparts by the end of the decade if current trends continue amid fears over mass job losses, the head of the European Union Chamber of Commerce in China has warned. In a case of “if you can’t beat them, join them”, Jens Eskelund said European companies operating in China were now thinking “Made in China for China” could be replaced by a philosophy of “Made in China for the world”.

At least 10 people died ⁠in a traffic accident involving about 50 vehicles on both ⁠sides of a foggy ⁠stretch of highway in southeastern Bulgaria this morning, the BTA ⁠news agency reported, citing the Yambol regional governor, Georgi Chalakov. Ch Insp Todor Mishinev from the Yambol regional directorate of the ministry of internal affairs told Nova TV that some people were still trapped ⁠in their cars.

Hungarian authorities have detained the brother of Viktor Orbán as part of a people-smuggling ⁠investigation, the prime minister, Péter Magyar, has said. The Hungarian anti-graft body, the national asset protection and recovery office (NVVH), said in ⁠a statement it and ⁠police had detained four people and searched homes in Budapest and Pest county.

Portugal will shut schools and non-esesential public services on Wednesday, with Storm Charles expected to bring torrential rain and heavy winds to parts of the country. “All those who can should stay at home,” the country’s interior minister Luis Neves told a press conference on Tuesday, warning people to stay away from coastal areas and to work from home where possible.
The European Union will contribute €50m ($55m) to an initiative to improve Black Sea security, EU chief Ursula von der Leyen said Tuesday, after several attacks on ships in the region.
A number of vessels were struck in the Black Sea off Bulgaria and Romania in October, leaving more than 30 sailors dead or missing, in suspected spillover from the Russia-Ukraine war.
During a visit to Bulgaria on Tuesday, von der Leyen said the EU wants to “fast track” the Black Sea Maritime Security Hub and agree “clear timelines for its completion”.
“And we want to offer dedicated funding of 50 million euros” to the initiative, she said.
The hub was proposed in 2025 as a joint Romanian-Bulgarian initiative to boost European presence in the area and counter Russian influence in the wake of Moscow’s 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
Von der Leyen also said €10m would be immediately allocated to Bulgarian search and rescue, following a similar announcement in Romania on Monday.

Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that the first day of US-led talks in Abu Dhabi between Ukraine and Russia was “constructive and quite substantive”, after being briefed by Kyiv’s negotiators in UAE.

“The trilateral format was constructive and quite substantive,” Zelensky said on X, adding that he “gave our team clear instructions for further dialogue – both in the trilateral format tomorrow and more broadly, over the coming days, with envoys of the US President and representatives of Europe.”
Trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi addressed humanitarian issues, Zelenskyy says
The Reuters news agency has some quotes from Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who has been speaking to students during his visit to Denmark.

Asked about the Abu Dhabi trilateral talks, he ⁠said ⁠that humanitarian issues such as ⁠prisoner of war exchanges ⁠and bringing back children had been discussed, adding that security guarantees were also on the agenda.
Zelenskyy arrived in Copenhagen earlier today for talks with Nordic leaders on military assistance, air defences and protecting Ukraine’s energy infrastructure from Russian strikes.
Denmark announced a donation of 4.8bn kroner ($720m; £537m) in military aid, but did not disclose which weapons or equipment would be included or when they would be delivered.

Amid relentless Russian attacks, Zelenskyy has been urging allies to accelerate deliveries of Patriot interceptor missiles – by far the most effective weapon available to Ukraine for downing Russia’s deadly ballistic missiles.

Europe’s manufacturers could give up on attempting to compete with their Chinese counterparts by the end of the decade if current trends continue amid fears over mass job losses, the head of the European Union Chamber of Commerce in China has warned.

In a case of “if you can’t beat them, join them”, Jens Eskelund said European companies operating in China were now thinking “Made in China for China” could be replaced by a philosophy of “Made in China for the world”.

Eskelund, who heads the influential Beijing-headquartered body, said European manufacturers could find themselves at an existential crossroads by the end of the decade, asking themselves: “What is the point of trading?”

As the EU gets tough with China with a deficit running at a record £1bn (€1.18bn) a day and an increasing mood for protectionism in Brussels, Berlin and Paris, he said European countries might need to shift their policies to allow domestic manufacturers to become part of Chinese firms’ supply chains, rather than treat them as competitors.

Iran rejects French claim it was behind supermarket fridge cyber-attack
Iran has responded to the accusation by France that it was responsible for the recent cyber-attacks on supermarket fridges in the European country, declaring them “baseless”.

AFP reports that in a statement, Tehran said “Iran’s foreign ministry categorically rejects the French government’s baseless and one-sided accusations against Iran regarding alleged cyber activities in France”, adding that it “strongly condemns this hackneyed policy of levelling accusations against the Islamic republic”.
Talks between Russia, Ukraine and US end after four hours
The first day of talks between Russia, Ukraine and the US in the UAE have ended after four hours.

The press office of the Foreign Intelligence Service of Ukraine has stated they are expected to resume tomorrow. The Ukrainian delegation has also spoken to representatives from Nato and Europe as part of their mission.
We reported in an earlier post that ten people had been killed after dozens of vehicles were involved in a traffic accident on the Trakia motorway in south-eastern Bulgaria.

In an update, Bulgaria’s health minister, Katya Ivkova, said 10 people died at the scene and two others died while being transported to hospital, bringing the total deaths to 12. She said 46 other people were transported to medical facilities for treatment.
The EU’s climate chief, Wopke Hoekstra, has admitted that expectations were “low” from the Cop31 summit in Turkey this year, but said there was hope for “meaningful” progress on clean electricity.
